flawed_step: Step 7: pairwise distinct individual arc capacities do not imply that distinct cuts have different total capacities.
counterexample: Take vertices {s,u,v,t} and arcs s→u, u→v, u→t, v→t with capacities 3,1,2,4 respectively. The four cut capacities are c({s})=3, c({s,u})=3, c({s,v})=7, and c({s,u,v})=6. Thus {s} and {s,u} are distinct minimum cuts. A positive flow exists (indeed, the maximum flow is 3).
assessment_summary:
Complete proof attempt and audit:

1. [JUSTIFIED] Label the two vertices other than s and t by u and v. This follows because the network has exactly four vertices.

2. [JUSTIFIED] The only s-t cuts are {s}, {s,u}, {s,v}, and {s,u,v}. Every cut must contain s, exclude t, and independently include or exclude u and v.

3. [JUSTIFIED] Let λ be the minimum of the capacities of these four cuts. The finite nonempty collection of cuts has a minimum.

4. [JUSTIFIED] To prove uniqueness, suppose that A and B are two distinct cuts of capacity λ and seek a contradiction. This is a valid contradiction setup.

5. [JUSTIFIED] Cut capacity is submodular: c(A)+c(B) ≥ c(A∩B)+c(A∪B). This follows by checking each directed arc’s contribution to the four cut capacities.

6. [JUSTIFIED] Both A∩B and A∪B are s-t cuts, so their capacities are at least λ; Step 5 therefore forces both to have capacity λ. Indeed, 2λ≥c(A∩B)+c(A∪B)≥2λ.

7. [NOT JUSTIFIED] Claim that pairwise distinct arc capacities make Step 6 impossible when A≠B. Distinct individual capacities do not prevent different sums of capacities from being equal; moreover, for nested A and B, the submodular equality gives no contradiction at all.

8. [NOT JUSTIFIED] Conclude that the minimum cut is unique. This depends entirely on the false claim in Step 7.

9. [JUSTIFIED] To test the failed claim, consider the network with vertices {s,u,v,t} and arcs s→u, u→v, u→t, v→t of capacities 3,1,2,4. It satisfies the loopless-digraph and pairwise-distinct-positive-integer requirements.

10. [JUSTIFIED] Its cut capacities are c({s})=3, c({s,u})=1+2=3, c({s,v})=3+4=7, and c({s,u,v})=2+4=6, directly from the definition of cut capacity.

11. [JUSTIFIED] Its maximum s-t flow is positive: send two units along s→u→t and one along s→u→v→t. This is a feasible flow of value 3 (and the cut {s} bounds every flow by 3).

12. [JUSTIFIED] Hence {s} and {s,u} are two distinct minimum cuts, so the proposed universal statement is false.
